cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Stranger – A person whom one does not know or with whom one is not familiar.

p.em: Example: Hooking up with a stranger sounds romantic until your true crime brain kicks in.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dangerous – Able or likely to cause harm or injury.

p.em: Example: She convinced herself that a mild-mannered guy named Scott was a dangerous serial killer.

cosy-blockquote.p: Paranoia – Unjustified suspicion and mistrust of other people.

p.em: Example: Watching too many murder documentaries induces acute, hilarious paranoia.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hotel – An establishment providing accommodation, meals, and other services.

p.em: Example: A neutral hotel room feels like a crime scene waiting to happen when you are anxious.

cosy-blockquote.p: Murderer – A person who commits murder.

p.em: Example: Every strange noise made her suspect he was secretly an escaped murderer.

cosy-blockquote.p: Excitement – A feeling of great enthusiasm and eagerness.

p.em: Example: The initial excitement of casual dating was completely drowned out by fear.

cosy-blockquote.p: Safe – Protected from or not exposed to danger or risk.

p.em: Example: She texted her best friend her exact GPS location just to feel safe.

cosy-blockquote.p: Intimacy – Close familiarity or friendship; closeness.

p.em: Example: Attempting physical intimacy with someone whose last name you don't know is awkward.

cosy-blockquote.p: Kidney – Either of a pair of organs that filter blood, often featured in urban legends.

p.em: Example: She worried she would wake up in an ice bath missing an entire kidney.

cosy-blockquote.p: Awkward – Causing or feeling embarrassment or inconvenience.

p.em: Example: Navigating small talk with a stranger in a quiet bedroom is deeply awkward.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: She is afraid from the stranger → Correct: She is afraid of the stranger ((Use 'afraid of' when expressing fear toward someone or something.))
Incorrect: He must to be a murderer → Correct: He must be a murderer ((Do not use 'to' after modal auxiliary 'must'.))
Incorrect: She wants to feel safely in the room → Correct: She wants to feel safe in the room ((Use predicate adjective 'safe' after linking verb 'feel'.))
